children: Australian stocks are shaping up to give back their recent hard-won gains when the market opens, following declines by U.S. equities. Local futures are down by 1.2% ahead of Thursday's session, suggesting that the S&P/ASX 200 is on track to give back the 1.1% gain compiled across the past six sessions. If the benchmark index performs in line with futures, it could finish below the three-month low it touched early last week. Ahead of the open, investment house Washington H. Soul Pattinson raised its final dividend despite a 10% slip in annual operating profit. U.S. stocks fell as the 10-year Treasury yield jumped back over 5% to the highest level since 2007. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite lost 1.1%, the DJIA dropped 0.7%, and the S&P 500 fell 0.75%. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
